title: あの＋名詞 — “that ～ (over there)”
summary: あの points to a thing or person that is far from both the speaker and the listener. It always comes directly before a noun. The set is この (near me), その (near you), あの (far from both), どの (which).

patterns.gloss: that ～ over there (あの山, あの人)
あの棚のお菓子 (the sweets on that shelf)

body.p: Use あの for things far from both people: あの山, あの人. If the thing is close to you, use この; if it is close to the listener, use その.
あの cannot stand alone. To point to the thing itself, use あれ (that one). あの本 = that book; あれ = that one.
あの is also a filler when you start talking: あの、すみません (um, excuse me). It then has no distance meaning.

examples.ja: あの たなの おかしを ください。
examples.romaji: Ano tana no okashi o kudasai.
examples.tr: Please give me the sweets on that shelf (over there).

examples.ja: あの山（やま）はとても高（たか）いです。
examples.romaji: Ano yama wa totemo takai desu.
examples.tr: That mountain over there is very tall.

examples.ja: あの人（ひと）は先生（せんせい）です。
examples.tr: That person over there is a teacher.

pitfalls: あの needs a noun after it. Say あれはなんですか, not あのはなんですか.
Do not mix up あの (far from both) and その (near the listener).
